title: Identity & Keying Phased Acceptance Playbook and Incident Evidence Protocol
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Purpose: Provide a pragmatic, phased sign-off playbook for Identity (SSO/SAML), Authorization (RBAC), and Keying (KMS/HSM) for Private/VPC deployments. This ticket captures: 1) acceptance gates per phase (staging -> canary -> GA), 2) required evidence artifacts for audits, 3) operator and customer runbooks for emergency keying/rotation, and 4) the decision/rollback rules for scope changes. The doc is intended for PMs, Eng leads, Security, and Customer Onboarding teams.
acceptance_criteria:
1) SSO: SAML federation validated with at least two IdP vendors (Okta, Azure AD) using test tenants; automated smoke test runs nightly.
2) RBAC: Role mapping documented and tested for least-privilege templates (Admin, DevOps, Operator, ReadOnly) with a successful impersonation audit test.
3) KMS/HSM: Customer-managed key import and rotation workflow executed in staging; HSM-backed asymmetric signing validated with quorum checks.
4) Audit logs: Retention and immutability verified (write-once storage verified for 90 days); end-to-end evidence available in audit snapshot.
5) Operator controls: Break-glass process documented and dry-run completed with on-call.
6) Canary: Canary rollout did not show any auth/crypto errors at 99.9%% P95 latency and passed smoke tests for 48 hours.
7) Documentation: Confluence PRD, runbook, and onboarding checklist reviewed and signed by Security and Legal.
8) Regression: No high-severity regressions in inference path caused by crypto integration for a minimum 72-hour observation window.
signoff_checklist: Security review sign-off (security@redwood) with evidence bundle ID
SAML metadata and fingerprint uploaded to customer onboarding portal
RBAC templates (Admin/Operator/Service) published and tested against sample tenants
KMS integration test: symmetric and asymmetric encryption/decryption success logs
HSM key import verification and attestation report attached
Audit log snapshot generated and checksum stored in evidence bucket
Failover test: KMS primary -> secondary switch validated and documented
Operational playbook validated with on-call (dry-run) including escalation contacts
Legal and Compliance acceptance for retention policy and cross-border key movement
Customer-facing onboarding checklist created and linked
notes:
Scope decisions and trade-offs: We will initially support IdP federation and SAML 2.0 flows; OIDC is planned in Phase 2 to reduce scope risk for this release. We agreed to postpone fine-grained attribute-based access control (ABAC) to a follow-up ticket to keep the MVP deliverable for Q2.
Trade-offs documented: Using cloud KMS with HSM attestation for MVP simplifies onboarding but requires strict audit snapshots and explanatory docs for enterprise buyers reluctant to host keys off-prem.
Operational constraints: Canary will be limited to a single region and reserved Dedicated capacity pool to isolate perf noise during crypto integrations.
